Description: Leaves of xantha-f26(M632R) seedlings greened at 320 μE m–2 s–1 or higher light intensities contained 8–10% of the chlorophyll accumulated in wild type leaves. The xantha-f60(P393L) mutation is leaky, but not as pronounced as xantha-f26. Leaves of xantha-f60 accumulate only trace amounts of protochlorophyllide in the dark and chlorophyll in the light. Therefore, the phenotype has to be explained by a reduced enzymatic activity. Less than 1% of the wild type activity was recorded with the modified subunit.

The missense mutation of xantha-f68 causes a G794E exchange in the protein. The mutation might cause structural damage to the protein since conserved glycine residues are often found in loops between secondary structural elements of proteins. Due to their unique size they cannot be exchanged by any other amino acid residue at these positions. The structurally damaged XAN-F protein is expected to be less stable in the xantha-f68 mutant plant, which could explain the significantly reduced amount of the XAN-F polypeptide found in the western blot analysis.
